definitions.explanation: The act of using one thing in place of another. Refers to both the process of substituting and the substitute itself.

examples.japanese: {代替|だいたい}{案|あん}を{出|だ}してください。
{電車|でんしゃ}が{止|と}まったので、{代替|だいたい}バスが{運行|うんこう}された。
examples.english: Since the trains stopped, substitute buses were operated.

examples.japanese: {化石|かせき}{燃料|ねんりょう}を{再生可能|さいせいかのう}エネルギーで{代替|だいたい}する{動|うご}きが{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: The movement to replace fossil fuels with renewable energy is advancing.

notes:
The traditional reading is だいたい, but the reading だいがえ has become common in spoken Japanese. Both are accepted, though だいたい remains standard in formal and written contexts. Not to be confused with the adverb {大体|だいたい} (roughly, approximately), which is a different word entirely.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{代替|だいたい}{案|あん} (alternative plan)
・{代替|だいたい}{手段|しゅだん} (alternative means)
・{代替|だいたい}{品|ひん} (substitute product)
・{代替|だいたい}エネルギー (alternative energy)
・{代替|だいたい}{交通|こうつう} (substitute transportation)
